brief.headline: Benito has new evening confusion with a stove safety event, an 8.6% weight loss since Sep 5, and low mood with missed day center days. These all appeared after his Oct 21 hospital admission.

items.statement: On 2026-11-17 the RN documented about two weeks of increased evening confusion, with the stove left on once. He was oriented to person and place but not date, and had no fever. Plan was urinalysis, medication review and a PCP visit that week. The PCP note of 2026-11-19 says only that chronic conditions are stable, and no urinalysis result is in the notes.
items.verifier_note: The 11/17 RN note and the 11/19 PCP note match every detail. The cited notes contain no urinalysis result.

items.statement: Weight fell from 96.9 kg (2026-09-05) to 94.0 kg (10/01), 91.1 kg (10/28) and 88.6 kg (11/24). That is 8.3 kg (18.3 lb), or 8.6%, in about 12 weeks. On 11/24 the dietitian noted poor appetite, skipped breakfast and about 50% of day center lunches eaten. Plan is a supplement twice daily, weekly weights and a dental check.
items.verifier_note: The weights and the change (-8.3 kg, -18.3 lb, -8.6%) match the vitals record. The dietitian note supports the appetite findings and the plan. The span is about 11.5 weeks, which fits 'about 12 weeks'.

items.statement: He missed 4 of the last 8 scheduled day center days (note of 2026-11-21). When present he is quiet and leaves activities early. On 11/23 he told the social worker he feels "down" and does not want to leave the house since a close friend died last month. Depression screening and grief support are planned.
items.verifier_note: The attendance note and the social work note match the statement. Screening and grief support are in the plan.

items.statement: He was seen in the ED on 2026-10-21 for chest pain and admitted for 2 days. The cardiac workup was negative and no new medications were started. The PCP follow-up on 10/25 found him at baseline per his spouse, and the plan was close monitoring for two weeks.
items.verifier_note: The discharge summary, the 10/25 PCP note and the encounter record support the ED visit, the 2-day admission, the negative workup, no new medications, baseline per spouse, and two weeks of monitoring.

items.statement: The medication record shows no medications started or stopped since 2026-09-01. The RN noted on 11/16 that medications were taken as directed.
items.verifier_note: The medication record lists nothing started or stopped since 9/1. The 11/16 RN note says medications were taken as directed.

questions_for_team: Were the urinalysis and medication review from 11/17 completed, and what did they show? What is the plan to evaluate the new evening confusion?
What home safety measures are needed for the stove incident, and who is supporting the caregiver?
Does the team want to look at whether the weight loss, low mood, reduced day center attendance and confusion are related? How soon will the depression screen and dental check happen?
Should the post-hospital monitoring period be extended given the changes since the Oct 21 admission?
The active medication list shows two simvastatin strengths (10 mg and 20 mg). Should this be clarified during the medication review?

checks: Confirm the review window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30) and pull all encounters in it: ED visits, urgent care, hospital admissions, observation stays, and any discharges, with reasons and dates.

Medication reconciliation: compare active list to prior review. Note simvastatin 10 mg start on 2026-02-04 alongside simvastatin 20 mg (start 2006-10-08). Flag possible duplicate statin therapy or a dose change that was not reconciled, and confirm which statin dose the patient is actually taking.

Check for medication starts and stops in the window, especially antiplatelet (clopidogrel), beta-blocker (metoprolol succinate), and nitroglycerin spray use or refills, which may signal ischemic heart disease activity.
Ischemic heart disease follow-up: chest pain or angina episodes, nitroglycerin use frequency, cardiology visits, and any ECG or cardiac testing in the window.

Blood pressure trend across the window: review home and clinic readings against the hypertension diagnosis, and flag orthostatic symptoms, dizziness, or falls if readings are low or highly variable on metoprolol.

Kidney function: review eGFR and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio results since last review, given CKD stage 1 and diabetic kidney disease listed. Note that the stage label should be checked against the most recent eGFR, and flag any new labs or nephrology referrals.

Glycemic status: review HbA1c and fasting glucose results, since prediabetes and diabetic kidney disease are both listed. Clarify whether the diagnoses conflict and whether any glucose-lowering therapy is present (none on active list).
Lipid panel and statin adherence: review most recent LDL and any lipid results, and confirm statin adherence and tolerance (myalgias, GI symptoms).
Anemia follow-up: review most recent hemoglobin, CBC trend, and any iron or B12 studies, and check for bleeding signs given clopidogrel use and anemia history.

Weight and BMI trend across the window (obesity and metabolic syndrome listed); flag change of 5% or more and any related dietary or activity referrals. Also check caregiver situation, mood, cognition, and ADL/IADL function changes, plus attendance at PACE center and any care-plan items due (assessments, reassessments, or goals) before 2026-11-30.
